newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ATHERTON LEADS ENGLAND TOWARDS WIN OVER NZ.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ATHERTON LEADS ENGLAND TOWARDS WIN OVER NZ.

text.p: England captain Mike Atherton, with a brilliant unbeaten century, put England well on the way to achieving their target of 305 at lunch on Tuesday to win the third and final test against New Zealand.
Resuming at 118 for two, England lost only the wicket of night watchman Andrew Caddick in the morning, reaching 203 for three wickets. Atherton was 105 not out by the lunch break.
England need 102 more runs with seven wickets standing in the two afternoon sessions.
Atherton has turned the match into a personal triumph.
He carried his bat for 94 in the first innings and as a result has so far been on the field for the entire four days and one session of the match to date.

A win at Lancaster Park will be particularly satisfying for Atherton. His team were slammed by the media for only drawing the test series and losing the one-day series in the first leg of the tour against Zimbabwe.

England convincingly won the second test in Wellington to take a 1-0 lead in the series and if England wins on Tuesday they will only be the second England side to successfully chase over 300 in the last innings.
Atherton brought up his century with a classic straight drive and raised both arms briefly to acknowledge the crowd but then quickly settled back to concentrate on his innings.
The chanceless 100, his 11th in tests, came off 267 balls and included nine boundaries.
With him at the interval was Nasser Hussain on 24 who batted more assertively than the other batsmen.
England found batting easier than they had on Thursday, particularly against the left-arm spin of Daniel Vettori.
Australian umpire Darrell Hair was at the centre of a controversial incident when Caddick prodded forward to Vettori and the ball lodged between his bat and pad before bouncing on to his boot.
New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming lunged forward to take the catch but Hair gave Caddick not out. Shortly after, Caddick whacked Vettori for six.
New Zealand finally claimed Caddick when he slammed Simon Doull to short mid wicket where Fleming, after a juggle, took the catch.
But Atherton and Hussain made steady progress towards the lunch break and increased the tempo when the second new ball was taken 25 minutes before the break.
